cards.front: In anatomical position, the palms face [___].
cards.context: In the standard anatomical position, the person stands upright with the upper limbs at the sides and the palms facing forward.

cards.front: The muscles of facial expression receive motor supply from [___].
cards.context: This is why a facial nerve lesion changes smiling, eye closure and forehead movement. The nerve also carries taste from the anterior tongue.

reference.title: Cranial Nerve Testing — Anatomy and Physiology; Technique

cards.front: Which large nerve divides into tibial and common fibular branches? [___]
cards.context: The division gives the lower limb its major posterior and lateral/anterior motor pathways. Proximal sciatic injury can therefore affect many movements.

reference.title: Anatomy, Bony Pelvis and Lower Limb: Tibial Nerve

cards.context: The lateral rectus lies on the temporal side of the globe. It moves the eye away from the nose and is supplied by the abducens nerve (CN VI).

reference.title: Cranial Nerves III, IV, and VI: Oculomotor Function

cards.front: Compared with a sixth-nerve nucleus lesion, an isolated peripheral sixth-nerve lesion preserves contralateral eye [___].
cards.context: A lesion of the peripheral sixth nerve weakens the ipsilateral lateral rectus. The opposite eye can still adduct because the contralateral medial rectus pathway is not part of that peripheral nerve.
